_comment: Every switchable option of the kit, in plain words. The setup questionnaire reads this file so the explanations live in one place. `kind` groups the options. `source` is the kit file or folder the option installs (rules and skills must have one); `installs` lists other kit files it copies. `default` is true/false for all profiles, or an object with solo/team/org. `controls` entries must agree with templates/scripts/workflow-config.mjs (the test checks it). `installAs` is the namespaced skill name in the user's project, so it never collides with a skill the user already has.

profiles.name: Solo
profiles.forWho: One owner who reads every diff and approves every step
profiles.summary: Light: warnings and advice. The goal is agreed before non-trivial work. Nothing blocks a commit except the hooks you choose to install.

profiles.name: Team
profiles.forWho: A few developers sharing a repository
profiles.summary: Adds a guard that protects existing tests during a bug fix and test-first for new logic. Review runs as advice.

profiles.name: Org
profiles.forWho: Many developers shipping in parallel, with policies that must hold
profiles.summary: Strict: the docs check blocks a commit, a clean review record is required to push, and success measurements are recorded.

options.title: Planning gates
options.what: Decides whether the assistant must agree the goal in writing (the Intent Anchor) before it builds anything non-trivial.
options.impact: off: the planner is used only when you ask. anchor: no code for non-trivial work until you approve the goal. full: also records success measurements. Routine small changes are exempt.

values.full: Goal agreed, plus success measurements recorded

options.title: Docs-fresh check at commit
options.what: At commit time, notices when source code changed but the project overview (AGENTS.md) did not.
options.impact: off: silent. warn: prints a reminder and lets the commit through. strict: blocks the commit until the overview is updated.

options.title: Instruction-file size warning
options.what: Warns when the always-loaded instruction files (CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md and similar) grow too large, since they cost context on every session.
options.impact: A number of characters; 0 turns the warning off. Informational only, never blocks.

options.title: Test-edit guard
options.what: During a bug fix, blocks the assistant from editing a test file that already exists in git, so a fix cannot be made to pass by weakening its own proof.
options.impact: off: no guard. on: a hook refuses edits to existing tests while fix mode is on. New test files are always allowed.

values.on: Existing tests are protected during a fix

options.title: Test-first policy
options.what: Tells the assistant when to write a failing test before the code.
options.impact: off: no rule. bugs: a bug fix starts with a failing test that reproduces it. on: new logic is test-first too. A plan bucket marked 'TDD: yes' opts in under any value except off.

values.bugs: Bug fixes start with a failing test
values.on: Bug fixes and new logic are test-first

options.title: End-to-end UI tests and screenshots
options.what: Lets the assistant test the interface the way a user would, and take screenshots of UI changes for the pull request.
options.impact: off: no end-to-end tests. browser: Playwright drives a headless browser; Playwright is installed in your project when you choose this. native (experimental): Maestro runs against a platform you supply and run yourself (Expo, Android Studio, Xcode or a device); the kit only prepares the way to connect it, and this path is not verified on a device. Works with or without the factory.

values.native: Experimental: Maestro against your own native platform (you supply and run it)

options.title: Independent review before push
options.what: A separate reviewer assistant reads the change cold, against the plan and a checklist (REVIEW.md), before it is committed.
options.impact: off: only when you ask. advisory: the review runs and the pre-push hook reminds you if there is no record. required: the pre-push hook blocks a push whose content has no clean review record.

values.advisory: Review runs; a missing record only produces a reminder
values.required: A push is blocked without a clean review record

options.title: Factory: automatic delivery after the plan
options.what: Once you approve the plan, agents and subagents carry the work through build, tests, review and commit without asking for each step, and can push and open the pull request.
options.impact: off: you drive every step (the default). local: everything up to the commits and the PR text, then it stops before any push. pr: also pushes a branch, opens the PR or a stack of PRs and watches CI. Nothing is ever merged or deployed; a person merges. The planning step still needs your approval.

values.local: Builds, tests, reviews and commits; stops before any push
values.pr: Also pushes, opens the PR or stack and watches CI; never merges

options.title: Factory: one PR or a stack
options.what: Decides how a plan with several features becomes pull requests.
options.impact: single: one PR for the whole plan. stack: one layer per bucket, each reviewable on its own. On GitHub this uses 'gh stack'; on GitLab it uses chained merge requests; where neither is available it opens one PR per bucket.

values.single: One PR for the whole plan

options.title: Factory: CI fix attempts
options.what: How many times the factory may fix a failing CI run and push again before it stops and tells you.
options.impact: A number; 0 means it only watches CI and reports. A cap keeps a broken pipeline from looping forever.
options.valueHint: number of attempts, 0 = watch and report only

options.title: Factory: code host
options.what: Which code host the factory pushes to and opens pull requests on.
options.impact: auto reads it from the git remote. github uses the gh command; gitlab uses glab. You sign in to the host yourself; the kit never stores a token.

values.auto: Read it from the git remote

options.title: Factory: confirm before pushing
options.what: Whether the factory pushes by itself or waits for your yes before each push. Only used when the factory is set to pr.
options.impact: auto: it pushes feature branches itself (the pre-push hook still refuses the protected branch). ask: it stops and asks before every push.

options.title: Factory: small documentation fixes without a subagent
options.what: Whether the factory may fix a tiny documentation-only problem itself (for example a CI check that wants a README line) instead of starting a builder and a reviewer. Only used when the factory is on.
options.impact: docs: a fix that touches only documentation files (Markdown, README, docs/, CHANGELOG) and at most 10 changed lines is made by the orchestrator, checked by `factory-guard.mjs fast-check`, verified, and labelled in the pull request as a self-checked fast fix; it saves a builder and a reviewer. off: every fix goes to a fresh builder and an independent re-review. Anything that touches code always goes to a builder.

values.off: Every fix goes to a builder and an independent re-review
values.docs: A tiny documentation-only fix is made and self-checked by the orchestrator

options.title: Checks that run Claude locally
options.what: Allows the two checks that call 'claude -p' on your machine (the @ import check and the skill trigger runner).
options.impact: They use your Claude usage, so they are opt-in and never run from hooks or CI.

values.true: Allowed when you run them by hand

options.title: Static config checks
options.what: Cheap checks that need no Claude: lint of the skill files and a resolver for @ imports.
options.impact: Free and fast; on in every profile.

options.title: Readable, self-documenting code
options.what: Full-word names, small functions, comments only for the why.
options.impact: The assistant rewrites cryptic names and long functions instead of adding explanations. Diffs may be slightly larger.
touches: always-on instruction file of each tool

options.title: Tidy repository
options.what: Every new file goes to the folder its kind belongs in, after looking for an existing helper to reuse.
options.impact: Fewer duplicate helpers and loose files; the assistant checks the overview for where things live.
touches: always-on instruction file of each tool

options.title: Keep the docs fresh
options.what: After every change the assistant updates the documents that describe it, in the same turn.
options.impact: Docs stay true without a separate cleanup task; every change touches a few more lines.
touches: always-on instruction file of each tool

options.title: Commit gate
options.what: The fixed order before every commit: fix lint, types and tests, update docs, review, then commit.
options.impact: Nothing is committed with failing checks; the assistant never skips the order to save time.
touches: always-on instruction file of each tool

options.title: Honest verification
options.what: The assistant says exactly what it ran and shows the result; code it only read is never called tested.
options.impact: Answers include the command and its output, and say plainly what was not checked.
touches: always-on instruction file of each tool

options.title: Test discipline
options.what: Failing test first for bug fixes (and new logic, depending on the profile), and no weakening a test to make it pass.
options.impact: Strictness follows the tests.tdd and tests.guard controls.
touches: always-on instruction file of each tool

options.title: Use the project's skills
options.what: When a task matches a skill, the assistant reads the whole skill before starting.
options.impact: Already part of the router; only needed on its own when the router is not installed.
touches: always-on instruction file of each tool

options.title: Flag user-visible UI changes
options.what: Each user-visible change adds a row to the design-sync list in the same turn.
options.impact: Needed so the design file can be brought up to date at the end of a session.
options.appliesWhen: The project has a UI and uses Figma
touches: always-on instruction file of each tool

options.title: Router
options.what: Sends each task to the right skill or document and holds the standing workflow rules.
options.impact: Makes the assistant consult the project's skills and truth order before changing code.

options.title: Goal-first planner
options.what: Interviews you for the real goal, then plans in small buckets with a checkpoint after each.
options.impact: Slows the start of big work slightly, in exchange for agreed scope and fewer rebuilds.

options.title: Pull request description
options.what: Writes a PR description from the real diff and commits, as copy-paste Markdown. Never opens or pushes the PR.
options.impact: Consistent, checked PR text; nothing is published without you.

options.title: Readable fix plan
options.what: Turns review findings or a bug list into one scannable plan with severity, verified file links and a checklist.
options.impact: Use when several findings need an order of work.

options.title: Harsh maintainability review
options.what: An extremely strict review of abstractions, giant files and growing condition chains. Runs only when you invoke it.
options.impact: No effect until you call it; the report can be long and blunt.

options.title: Project overview writer
options.what: Writes or refreshes AGENTS.md from the real code: architecture, stack, commands.
options.impact: Gives the assistant (and new people) an accurate map; the docs-fresh check relies on it.

options.title: Changelog and version bump
options.what: Keeps one CHANGELOG.md with an Unreleased section that each relevant commit adds to, and bumps the version on release.
options.impact: Every user-facing commit carries a changelog line. Optional commit hook and release workflow automate it.
touches: the file holding the version, e.g. package.json

options.title: Figma design sync
options.what: Turns the list of flagged UI changes into Figma frames at the end of a working session.
options.impact: Needs a Figma connection. Pointless for projects without a UI.
options.appliesWhen: The project has a UI and uses Figma

options.title: Setup (this questionnaire)
options.what: The installer prompt. It stays inside the kit folder and is not copied into the project's own skills.
options.impact: Run it again to change your choices; it is safe to repeat.

options.title: Pre-commit hook
options.what: Runs your lint, type and test commands, the changelog entry check and the docs-fresh check before each commit.
options.impact: Commits take a few seconds longer. It chains with an existing hook (husky or .git/hooks) and never replaces it.
touches: the project's pre-commit hook (a marked block)

options.title: Pre-push hook
options.what: Checks that the change has a review record before it is pushed.
options.impact: Reminder or hard stop depending on review.mode. Chains with an existing pre-push hook.
touches: the project's pre-push hook (a marked block)

options.title: Release version-bump workflow
options.what: A GitHub Actions workflow that bumps the version and finalizes the changelog when a release is made.
options.impact: Runs in CI on your repository; you review its branch, paths and version files before it is written.
options.appliesWhen: The project uses GitHub Actions and changelog-bump
touches: .github/workflows/release_bump.yaml (new file; existing workflows are never touched)

options.title: Review gate
options.what: A reviewer subagent, the REVIEW.md checklist and a review-record check, so a second reader examines every change.
options.impact: Adds one review step per change; how hard it is enforced is set by review.mode.

options.title: Reviewer guard: keep the reviewer read-only
options.what: A script and a Claude Code hook that stop the reviewer subagent from running anything except git status, diff, log and show and the project's lint, type check, test and build commands, one command per call. Without it the reviewer is only told not to change anything.
options.impact: Adds one PreToolUse hook on Bash to .claude/settings.json (your own hooks and keys are kept; setup tells you if the file has to be edited by hand). The hook acts only on the reviewer and lets every other call through. It is not a sandbox: a project's own test or build command can still write files. It fails open if it cannot read a call. Claude Code only; other tools keep the instruction-only limit.

options.title: Factory guard and builder
options.what: A script that decides whether an automatic delivery run (the factory) may start, lists what is left to build in the plan, counts CI fix attempts against a cap, refuses pushes to the protected branch, and writes a stop report; plus the builder subagent that builds one bucket of the plan in a fresh context.
options.impact: Only used when the factory is on (factory.mode is local or pr). It never merges or deploys. Keeps its counts and report in .claude/factory/, which is git-ignored. The builder subagent is a Claude Code feature.

options.title: End-to-end tests and screenshots
options.what: Sets up and runs end-to-end UI tests the way a user would, and takes screenshots for pull requests. Browser: Playwright in a headless browser (proven). Native (experimental): Maestro against a platform you supply and run yourself (Expo, Android Studio, Xcode or a device); written from the documentation and not verified on a device.
options.impact: Nothing runs until you set tests.e2e to browser or native. It asks before installing Playwright (about 40 seconds the first time). Works with or without the factory.

options.title: Run the factory
options.what: After you approve the plan, carries it through build, tests, review and commit with a fresh builder agent per bucket, then (in pr mode) pushes, opens the pull request or a stack of them and watches CI. Started only by you, with /wk-run-factory. Never merges or deploys.
options.impact: Nothing happens until you start it and set factory.mode to local or pr. It pushes only feature branches and stops at a cap on CI fixes. Needs the reviewer, the PR description skill and the factory guard, which are added for you.

options.title: Screenshot helper
options.what: A script that publishes the screenshots from an end-to-end run to a branch of their own and builds the Markdown that shows them in a pull request.
options.impact: Only used when you run end-to-end tests (tests.e2e is browser or native). The images never reach main or your feature branch; one extra branch, factory-screenshots, is pushed. It needs no Claude and no network apart from that push.
touches: the factory-screenshots branch on your remote

options.title: Config checks
options.what: Scripts that lint the skill files, resolve @ imports and report instruction-file size, plus a profile viewer.
options.impact: Run by hand or from a package script such as check:config. No Claude needed.

options.title: Claude-powered checks
options.what: A runner for the checks that call 'claude -p' (skill trigger tests, @ import verification).
options.impact: Uses your Claude usage and only runs when you start it and claude.runChecks allows it.

options.title: Test-edit guard script and hook
options.what: The script and tool hook behind the tests.guard control.
options.impact: Installed only when tests.guard is on (default in team and org).

options.title: Plan mode as the session default
options.what: Claude Code starts every session in plan mode, where it cannot edit files until you accept a plan.
options.impact: A hard stop behind the planning gate. Every session starts in plan mode, even trivial ones. Does not apply in the VS Code extension.

options.title: PLAN.md
options.what: A starting file for the Intent Anchor, bucket map and decision log that the planner keeps.
options.impact: Lets a new session resume where the last stopped. Created only if it does not exist.

options.title: BACKLOG.md
options.what: A starting file for ideas and later work, kept out of the current plan.
options.impact: Created only if it does not exist.

options.title: CLAUDE.md starter
options.what: A short always-on file for Claude Code that points to the overview and the rules.
options.impact: If CLAUDE.md exists, the kit adds only a marked block and leaves your text alone.
touches: CLAUDE.md (new file, or a marked block in the existing one)

options.title: Expo / React Native pack
options.what: Router rows and a rule that makes the assistant load the matching Expo skill before touching Expo, EAS or React Native APIs.
options.impact: Expo changes APIs every SDK, so this avoids answers from stale memory. Needs the Expo plugin or a repo-local copy of its skills.
touches: always-on instruction file of each tool

options.title: Expo: skill and docs first
options.what: Before Expo, EAS or React Native API work, the assistant loads the matching Expo skill once per session.
options.impact: Slightly slower first answer, far fewer outdated APIs.
touches: always-on instruction file of each tool
